cohort: 568 mother-child pairs from the Boston Birth Cohort, followed at the Boston Medical Center between 1998 and 2018, with a mean child age of 9.3 years at follow-up
finding: Higher cord levels of methionine, glycine, serine, and 8-hydroxy-deoxyguanosine were associated with significantly higher odds of childhood ADHD, with cord methionine and glycine statistically mediating the association between cord acetaminophen levels and ADHD.
